title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: Augustine Tract. 107/111 — world = those not in the lot of grace to be chosen out of it; those not given are those to whom Christ will not give eternal life = the passed-over alone
pass_a_gloss: Hence Tract. 107. in Evang. Joann. unto these words, I ask not for the world, but for these whom thou hast given me, he so writes; He wills the world to be understood as those who live according to the concupiscence of the world, and are not in that lot of grace that they be elected by him out of the world. And Tract. 111: They have not been given unto him, unto whom he will not give everlasting life. But who finally are those, unto whom Christ will not give everlasting life, except those, and those alone, whom we call the passed over, non-elect or reprobate? for unto all the elect he will give it.
pass_b_english: Hence on Tract. 107 on John's Gospel, at the words I ask not for the world, but for these whom you have given me, he writes: By world he means those who live by the world's lust, and are not in that lot of grace to be chosen by him out of the world. And Tract. 111: They have not been given to him to whom he will not give everlasting life. But who finally are those to whom Christ will not give everlasting life, except those — and those alone — whom we call the passed over, non-elect or reprobate? For to all the elect he will give it.
source_text: Hinc Tract. 107. in Evang. Joann. ad haec verba, Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro his quos dedisti mihi, sic scribit; Mundum vult intelligi, qui vivunt secundum concupiscentiam mundi, et non sunt in ea sorte gratiae ut ab illo eligantur ex mundo. Et Tract. 111: Non ei dati sunt, quibus vitam non dabit aeternam. At quinam tandem illi sunt, quibus Christus non dabit vitam aeternam, nisi illi, et illi soli, quos appellamus praeteritos, non-electos sive reprobatos? nam omnibus electis dabit eam.
